tasks.short: Run pension, collective insurance and savings schemes: process changes, check premium invoices, chase the pension fund and broker.

today.trigger: New hires, leavers, salary or part-time changes in AFAS, monthly premium invoices, broker or fund emails, employee questions.
steps: Pull the month's starters, leavers and salary changes from AFAS
Check that the pension declaration (UPA) and insurer data match AFAS
Reconcile pension and WIA/WGA insurance premium invoices against headcount and the payroll ledger
Email the broker or fund about differences and follow up
Answer employee questions on pension, the Wtp transition and insurance cover
drudgery: Retyping mutations into fund and broker portals
Chasing the same open differences by email for weeks
today.time_sinks: Monthly reconciliation of premium invoices against AFAS and repeated follow-up of the same differences with the fund and broker.

lenses.faster: A nightly comparison of AFAS against the fund and insurer data lists only the differences, so manual line checking disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Every AFAS mutation triggers a check and a draft notice to the broker; open differences are chased automatically after five working days.
lenses.ambitious: Every employee gets a clear personal overview of their pension and insurance cover after the Wtp transition, in Dutch and the main languages of the warehouse staff.
lenses.joy: No more invoice ticking; time goes to explaining pension choices to people who need it.
lenses.options: For each difference the agent proposes possible causes (date of entry, part-time factor, salary basis) ranked by likelihood.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the reconciliation rules and the exception queue instead of doing the reconciliation.
reach: Payroll Specialist: pension deduction checks at month close
Accountant: pension and insurance accruals in the general ledger
HR Administrator: first-line benefit questions

tasks.human_edge: Judging disputed cover cases, negotiating with the broker and explaining pension choices to anxious employees.
tasks.pattern_why: Several systems, recurring exceptions and outbound messages to third parties; the specialist approves corrections before they go to the fund or broker.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract and arrival of a premium invoice or fund report.
steps: Compare AFAS employment and salary data with the fund declaration and insurer lists
Match invoice lines to employees and flag differences above a threshold
Draft correction notices and broker emails with the evidence attached
Specialist approves or edits; agent sends and tracks the reply
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves every correction and outgoing message to the fund, insurer or broker.
data_needed: AFAS employment, salary and part-time data
Premium invoices and insurer member lists
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint reconciliation log per month with each difference, decision and message sent

evidence.claim: Excel and Power BI can do rule-based reconciliation of two datasets with no model involved
Microsoft 365 Copilot drafts emails in Outlook from context

risks: Pension and health-related data are sensitive under AVG; access must be limited
Wrong correction sent to the fund can affect an employee's pension accrual
Fund and broker portals may not offer exports, keeping manual steps
research_questions: How many differences per month does the current reconciliation find, and how many hours go into each?
Do the pension fund and broker provide machine-readable member lists or only PDFs?
Which differences recur every month and could be fixed at the source in AFAS?

tasks.short: Grade a new or changed job under the CAO grading system, check overtime and allowance rules, set the salary scale.

today.trigger: A manager asks for a new role or says an existing role has changed.
steps: Interview the manager and sometimes a jobholder
Write or update the job profile
Compare it with reference jobs in the CAO grading system
Decide the grade, overtime and shift-allowance eligibility and scale
Record the outcome in AFAS and inform the manager
drudgery: Writing profiles from scratch from rough notes
Searching the reference job handbook for comparable jobs
today.time_sinks: Turning interview notes into a profile in the right format and finding comparable reference jobs.

lenses.faster: The interview is transcribed and turned into a draft profile, and the three closest reference jobs are suggested, so writing and searching mostly disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A role change entered in AFAS starts a structured questionnaire to the manager before the specialist is involved.
lenses.ambitious: All roles across the three sites are checked for consistent grading, not only the ones someone asks about.
lenses.joy: Less copy-writing, more time on the judgement of what the job really is.
lenses.options: For each role, two or three plausible grades with the arguments for each, so the specialist sees the borderline clearly.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the job architecture and grading rules and reviews AI-prepared proposals.
reach: HR Business Partner: first conversation with managers on role design
Recruiter: vacancy text built from the approved profile

tasks.human_edge: The grading decision itself, which sets pay, has to be defensible to the employee, the works council and the CAO grading committee.
tasks.pattern_why: The grade affects pay and is a decision on terms of employment; under the EU AI Act such use is high-risk, so AI prepares and the person decides.

in_practice.trigger: Manager submits a role request or change form.
steps: Manager completes a structured questionnaire; optional recorded interview is transcribed
Copilot drafts the job profile in the company format
Copilot lists the closest reference jobs and the grading factors that differ
Specialist decides the grade and scale and records it in AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist (and grading committee where the CAO requires it) decides the grade.
data_needed: CAO grading manual and reference jobs
in_practice.logs_to: Job profile file on SharePoint with draft, sources and final grading rationale

evidence.claim: Teams transcribes meetings and Copilot summarises them into documents
Matching a draft profile to the closest reference jobs from a handbook is a retrieval task language models do well

risks: Model may copy reference job wording, making profiles look more alike than the jobs are
EU AI Act high-risk obligations if the tool's suggestion is used as the decision
Gender bias in profile wording may carry into grades, a concern under the EU Pay Transparency Directive
research_questions: Does the CAO grading method allow digital tools in the grading procedure, and does the works council need to be consulted?
How often does the specialist's final grade differ from the closest reference job suggested?
How many role requests come in per year per site?

tasks.short: Research benefit and safety practices and the law, and propose changes to our schemes and policies.

today.trigger: Law or CAO change, Wtp transition, renewal of an insurance contract, a question from the HR Director or the works council.
steps: Read sources: CAO texts, government sites, broker notes, sector reports
Compare our schemes with the market and the sector
Estimate costs of options in Excel
Write a memo and recommendation for the HR Director
Prepare the works council consent request where needed
drudgery: Reading long legal and sector documents for a few relevant paragraphs
today.time_sinks: Collecting and summarising sources before any real analysis starts.

lenses.faster: A research assistant collects and summarises sources with citations, and drafts the comparison table, cutting days of reading to hours of checking.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly watch on legislation, CAO and sector pension news produces a short digest of what affects Noordhaven.
lenses.ambitious: Every scheme is reviewed on a fixed cycle, including flex workers' coverage and shift-work health risks, instead of only when something breaks.
lenses.joy: Less skimming of documents, more time on the trade-offs and on talking to employees about what they value.
lenses.options: Three to five policy options per question, each with cost, employee impact and works council implications.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets the research questions and checks sources and conclusions rather than gathering material.
reach: HR Director: drafting the policy case
People Analytics: benefit uptake analysis
FP&A Analyst: cost estimates of benefit changes

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what fits Noordhaven's people and budget, and steering the proposal through management and the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: Open-ended research where the person sets the question and owns the recommendation.

in_practice.trigger: Policy question, law change alert or contract renewal date.
steps: Specialist states the question and constraints
Research assistant gathers sources with citations and summarises them
Copilot drafts option table with cost estimates from AFAS data
Specialist checks sources, chooses recommendation and finalises the memo
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist verifies every cited source and signs the recommendation.
in_practice.logs_to: Policy research folder on SharePoint with sources, options and decision

evidence.claim: AI research features gather web sources and write cited summaries

risks: Invented or outdated legal references
US-centric sources creeping into Dutch policy advice
Over-reliance on summaries without reading the actual CAO text
research_questions: What share of research time goes to gathering versus analysis today?
How often do summaries contain errors on Dutch law when checked against the source?
Which policy reviews are overdue because there was no time?

tasks.short: Answer manager and employee questions on the CAO, pay, allowances, leave, pension and HR procedures.

today.trigger: Email, Teams message or phone call from a manager, employee or HR colleague.
steps: Understand the question and the employee's situation
Look up the CAO article, policy or AFAS record
Write or give the answer
Follow up if the answer leads to a change in AFAS
drudgery: Answering the same shift-allowance and leave questions over and over
Searching two CAOs and many policies for the right article
today.time_sinks: Repeat questions and looking up articles across two CAOs and SharePoint policies.

lenses.faster: A Teams assistant answers with the exact CAO article cited, and the specialist only reviews complex cases.
lenses.autonomous: Routine questions on allowances, leave and procedures are answered directly with citations; anything about an individual's pay or a dispute goes to the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Shift workers get answers in their own language at any hour, including flex workers on what applies to them.
lenses.joy: No more copy-pasting the same answer; the specialist handles the interesting and sensitive cases.
lenses.options: For ambiguous cases, the assistant shows the possible readings of the CAO article for the specialist to choose.
lenses.altitude: The specialist curates the knowledge base and reviews logged answers for errors and gaps.
reach: HR Business Partner: first-line CAO questions from managers
HR Administrator: routine procedure questions
Payroll Specialist: questions about payslip components

tasks.human_edge: Sensitive or individual situations, disputes and advice that carries legal risk.
tasks.pattern_why: Retrieval over CAOs and policies plus routing; the specialist approves answers at first, then only handles flagged exceptions.

in_practice.trigger: Question posted in the HR Teams channel or sent to the HR mailbox.
steps: Assistant classifies the question and retrieves the relevant CAO article and policy
Assistant drafts an answer with citations
Low-risk general questions are answered after review; individual or legal ones go to the specialist
Unanswered or corrected questions update the knowledge base
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves draft answers; after a tested period, only flagged categories need approval.
in_practice.logs_to: Question log with answer, sources, reviewer and corrections

evidence.claim: Copilot Studio builds Teams agents grounded on SharePoint content

risks: Wrong answer on pay or rights treated as a company commitment
Assistant answering for the wrong CAO (transport versus warehouse)
Personal data in questions processed outside agreed AVG boundaries
research_questions: What share of incoming questions are general versus about an individual case?
How accurate is a grounded assistant on a test set of 100 real questions from the past year?
Does the works council want a say on an employee-facing HR assistant?

tasks.short: Design and run the annual pay round, merit and bonus schemes, and the CAO step increases.

today.trigger: Annual pay review cycle, CAO wage increase, bonus year-end.
steps: Prepare budget and Excel templates per manager from AFAS data
Send templates and chase managers
Check proposals against budget, scales and rules
Get approval from HR Director and Finance
Load approved changes into AFAS before payroll close
drudgery: Checking returned sheets for formula and rule errors
today.time_sinks: Template preparation, chasing managers and validating returned spreadsheets.

lenses.faster: One central tool with built-in rules replaces per-manager workbooks, and checks and the AFAS import file are generated automatically.
lenses.autonomous: CAO step increases and indexation run as rules on the AFAS data with an exception list; reminders to managers go out on schedule.
lenses.ambitious: Proper pay-equity checks by gender and site in every cycle, ready for pay transparency reporting.
lenses.joy: No spreadsheet chasing; the work becomes designing the scheme and coaching managers on fair choices.
lenses.options: Budget scenarios (e.g. 2, 3 and 4 percent merit pot, different distributions) modelled side by side.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the scheme rules and the tool, and reviews outliers rather than every line.
reach: Payroll Specialist: preparing salary mutations for AFAS
FP&A Analyst: personnel cost forecast from the pay round
People Analytics: pay-equity analysis

tasks.human_edge: Scheme design, judging fairness of individual outliers and negotiating budgets with management.
tasks.pattern_why: Rules for scales, steps, budgets and validations can be written down and checked; no model is needed at run time.

in_practice.trigger: Pay cycle start date or new CAO wage table.
steps: Load AFAS employee, scale and salary data into the pay-round tool
Apply CAO steps and rules automatically; managers enter merit proposals in a controlled form
Tool validates against budget and scale limits and flags outliers and equity gaps
Specialist reviews exceptions; approved file is imported into AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and HR Director approve the final file before AFAS import.
in_practice.logs_to: Pay-round audit file with each proposal, approval and import batch

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports importing salary mutations from files
AI coding assistants can build validation tools of this size quickly

risks: Rule errors applied at scale to all employees
Performance ratings used in pay decisions may need works council consent
Managers working around the tool in side spreadsheets
research_questions: How many hours go into the pay cycle across HR, payroll and managers today?
Which rules in the current workbooks are undocumented and live only in formulas?
Can AFAS take a clean import of all mutations, or are some entered by hand?

tasks.short: Advise on employee objections to their grade or salary and prepare the case for the objection committee.

today.trigger: An employee or manager files an objection to a grade or salary.
steps: Collect the job profile, grading file and salary history
Talk with the employee and manager
Compare with reference jobs and similar colleagues
Write advice for the HR Director or the CAO objection committee
Explain the outcome to the employee
drudgery: Assembling the case file from several places
Writing the advice in the required format
today.time_sinks: Gathering documents and comparable cases before the actual assessment.

lenses.faster: The case file and comparable cases are assembled automatically, and a first draft of the advice follows the CAO procedure format.
lenses.autonomous: Filing an objection opens a case with deadlines from the CAO procedure tracked automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Patterns across objections are analysed to fix grading weaknesses before more complaints arise.
lenses.joy: Less paperwork, more time for the conversation with the employee.
lenses.options: The draft shows arguments for upholding and for rejecting the objection side by side.
lenses.altitude: The specialist reviews prepared cases and improves the grading system based on objection patterns.
reach: HR Business Partner: preparing employee conversations
HR Director: committee secretariat

tasks.human_edge: Hearing the employee, weighing fairness, and owning an outcome that affects pay and trust.
tasks.pattern_why: Although scored as automatable, this is a pay decision about a person; AI Act high-risk rules and trust keep the person in charge while AI prepares the file and draft.

in_practice.trigger: Objection received by email or form.
steps: Open a case and set CAO procedure deadlines
Pull profile, grading rationale, salary history and comparable roles
Draft advice with both sides of the argument
Specialist meets the parties, decides the advice and finalises it
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist writes the final advice; committee or HR Director decides.
in_practice.logs_to: Confidential case folder on SharePoint with access limited to HR and the committee

evidence.claim: Copilot in Word drafts documents from files the user points to

risks: Comparison with named colleagues' pay exposes personal data
An AI-drafted advice may be seen as the decision, undermining the procedure
Few cases per year limits learning and checking
research_questions: How many objections are filed per year and how long does each take?
Does the CAO objection procedure set rules on what evidence may be used?
Would employees and the works council accept AI-prepared case files?

tasks.short: Write and maintain job profiles, the job catalogue and salary scales for both CAOs.

today.trigger: New roles, reorganisations, CAO wage table changes, outdated profiles.
steps: Collect input from managers and existing profiles
Write or update profiles in the standard format
Update scale tables after a CAO increase
Publish on SharePoint and update AFAS
drudgery: Updating scale tables by hand in several places
today.time_sinks: Keeping hundreds of profiles consistent and current across three sites.

lenses.faster: Profiles are drafted in the standard format from manager input, and scale tables are generated from the CAO wage table in one step.
lenses.autonomous: A new CAO wage table updates all scale tables and the AFAS import file, with a diff for review.
lenses.ambitious: A complete, current job catalogue for all three sites, also translated for non-Dutch staff, for the first time.
lenses.joy: No reformatting; the work is about getting the content of jobs right.
lenses.options: Two or three wording variants for profiles, including a gender-neutral check.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the job architecture and the templates and checks AI drafts.
reach: Recruiter: vacancy texts from profiles
L&D Specialist: required certificates linked to each profile

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what a job really contains and agreeing it with managers.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured manager input becomes a structured profile in a fixed template; scale tables are deterministic.

in_practice.trigger: Profile request, reorganisation or new CAO wage table.
steps: Model drafts profile in the template from questionnaire and old profile
Consistency and bias check against the catalogue
Scale tables computed from the CAO wage table by script
Specialist approves and publishes to SharePoint and AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves each profile and the updated scale tables.

evidence.claim: Language models produce structured documents in a given template

risks: Generic profiles that do not reflect real warehouse or transport work
Scale errors after script changes if not tested
research_questions: How many profiles exist and how many are older than three years?
Do managers recognise AI-drafted profiles as accurate in a test of ten roles?
Where are scale tables duplicated today?

tasks.short: Cost out CAO wage proposals, allowances and pension changes for negotiations and budgets.

today.trigger: Warehouse CAO negotiations, sector CAO outcome, budget round.
steps: Extract salary, hours and allowance data from AFAS
Build the cost model in Excel
Calculate scenarios for union and employer proposals
Present results to HR Director, Finance Director and the negotiation team
drudgery: Rebuilding the model for each new proposal during talks
today.time_sinks: Re-running scenarios by hand under time pressure during negotiations.

lenses.faster: A reusable cost model on the nightly AFAS extract recalculates any proposal in minutes.
lenses.autonomous: The model refreshes nightly so the baseline is always current.
lenses.ambitious: Live costing during negotiation sessions, including flex worker costs and shift patterns.
lenses.joy: No late-night spreadsheet rebuilding; time goes into understanding what the proposals mean.
lenses.options: Many scenarios side by side: wage increase, allowance changes, pension premium, timing.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs and checks the model rather than building it each round.
reach: FP&A Analyst: personnel cost forecasting
Controller: wage cost accruals

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting results for negotiators and judging what is affordable and fair.
tasks.pattern_why: Cost formulas are known and checkable; build once with AI coding help and run without a model.

steps: Load baseline from nightly AFAS extract
Enter proposal parameters
Model computes costs per site, CAO and year
Specialist checks and presents results
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist checks the model output before it goes to negotiators.

evidence.claim: AI coding assistants help build such models quickly

risks: Model errors carried into negotiations
Data in the AFAS extract incomplete for allowances
research_questions: How long did the last round of costing take?
Does the nightly extract hold all allowance data?
Would negotiators use live scenarios in the room?

role.altitude: From doing benefit admin, grading and pay rounds by hand to owning Noordhaven's reward rules, job catalogue and cost models, and checking the tools that run them.
reach: Payroll Specialist: pension and salary mutation checks
FP&A Analyst: personnel cost forecasts
People Analytics: pay-equity and benefit uptake reports
HR Business Partner: first-line CAO questions
Recruiter: vacancy texts from job profiles
role.ceiling_note: Limited by AFAS data quality, works council consent rights, EU AI Act high-risk rules on pay decisions, and the need for a person to own grading and complaint outcomes; perhaps 35-45% of hours can be freed.
skills_to_grow: Designing and testing rule-based tools and AI assistants
Power BI and data modelling on AFAS extracts
EU AI Act and AVG compliance for HR tools
role.ambitious_version: A single reward system for Noordhaven: current job catalogue, automatic CAO steps, live negotiation costing, pay-equity reporting and a cited CAO assistant for all staff, with the specialist as owner and auditor.
